rv.q: The awkward first 30 minutes of 'Soft Power' aren't musical at all, and we can tell from all the throat-clearing that the team feels hesitant about jumping into such a wild-spirited spoof…When Tesori's lush music starts, the play sighs with relief: Nothing, it turns out, buoys your post-2016 spirits like an orchestra in full swoon.

One feels fortunate to be alive in a time where artists from marginalized demographics are getting a long overdue platform to stage boldly authentic and incisive works, made by and for themselves. Recent shows like Slave Play and A Strange Loop have also demonstrated their economic viability.

3/5 Stars: "A frequently wry, extremely topical cheerfully mocking musical. Expertise, smarts, and speed gloss over the musical's lesser stretches and deliver a national lampoon likely to engage audiences who like their entertainment thoughtful."
3/5 Stars: "'Soft Power' is inventive, satiric, caustic and intriguing. But at some point-despite a joyfully singing and dancing Hillary Clinton-the fun stops as the fantasy runs aground."
